about: The acclamation adapts Saint John the Baptist's words in John 1:29. The Gospel's third-person singular qui tollit peccátum mundi becomes the direct address qui tollis peccáta mundi. According to the Liber Pontificalis, Pope Sergius I (687–701) ordered the clergy and people to sing it during the breaking of the Lord's Body.

seg.nr: The priest covers the chalice, genuflects and rises. Bowing before the Blessed Sacrament with joined hands, he says the Agnus Dei in an audible voice and strikes his breast three times — at each “miserére nobis” and at “dona nobis pacem”. At a sung Mass all the faithful sing it.

seg.tr: Lamb of God, You take away the sins of the world: have mercy on us.

fn.w001: Nominative used in direct address. The regular vocative would be agne.
fn.w004: Second-person singular. The relative qui refers to “Agnus” (w001).

seg.tr: Lamb of God, You take away the sins of the world: have mercy on us.
Lamb of God, You take away the sins of the world: grant us peace.

fn.w023: Imperative governing “nobis” (w024) in the dative and “pacem” (w025) in the accusative.

seg.nr: This rubric governs Masses for the Dead: there “dona eis réquiem” takes the place of “miserére nobis”, and the third time “dona eis réquiem sempitérnam”. At those Masses the priest does not strike his breast, and the kiss of peace is not given.
